rationale: The Latin anchor 'crementum' (growth, increase, that which grows) points to the botanical sense of seed as a plant ovule/reproductive unit capable of growth, which aligns precisely with seed.n.02 (a mature fertilized plant ovule). The attestations in glossaries (Wrt. Voc., Ælfc. Gl.) confirm a concrete botanical meaning, and seed.n.02 is more botanically precise than seed.n.01 (which refers to a small hard fruit rather than the ovule itself).
